episode.throughLine: A short source-led first-publication vignette: remembered café competition prompted a collaboration; the published song brought unexpectedly little money. No invented personal low, helper chain or recovery.

facts.statement: Irving Berlin was born May 11, 1888. His first published song appeared in 1907, when he was eighteen or nineteen. The candidate uses approximately nineteen, without claiming an exact composition or publication month.

sourceRefs.locator: Concise Biography, paragraphs beginning 'Irving Berlin was born' and 'In 1907'.
1907 copyright on first music page (image 077-181-001); cover credits I. Berlin.

facts.statement: In his attributed 1934 interview answer, Berlin said he wrote his first song in collaboration with the piano player at the café where he was a singing waiter.

sourceRefs.locator: Printed pp. 32–33, PDF p. 27: Berlin's attributed first-song answer starts in the final paragraph of p. 33 left column and continues at the top of p. 33 right column.

facts.statement: Berlin's attributed 1934 answer says competition prompted the collaboration: the singing waiter and pianist at the café across the street had written a hit.

sourceRefs.locator: Printed pp. 32–33, PDF p. 27: Berlin's attributed first-song answer starts in the final paragraph of p. 33 left column and continues at the top of p. 33 right column.

facts.statement: Marie from Sunny Italy was published in 1907 by Jos. W. Stern & Co.; the original cover and music page credit I. Berlin with words and M. Nicholson with music. The score is for piano and voice. The official biography identifies it as his first published song.

sourceRefs.locator: JHU Levy Collection Box 077, Item 181: original cover 077-181-000, first music page 077-181-001; catalog date, instrumentation and plate number 5682-3.

facts.statement: Berlin's attributed 1934 answer says the first song was not a hit, brought a profit of thirty-odd cents, and surprised him by this poor return. This recollected joint-profit figure is not equated with other accounts of individual royalties.

sourceRefs.locator: Printed pp. 32–33, PDF p. 27: Berlin's attributed first-song answer starts in the final paragraph of p. 33 left column and continues at the top of p. 33 right column.

facts.statement: Berlin wrote songs for performers, musical theatre and films.

sourceRefs.locator: Concise Biography, paragraphs beginning 'Over the next five decades', 'He was equally at home' and 'Among the Hollywood movie musical classics'.

arc.canonicalText: He was a singing waiter, about nineteen, when he worked on his first published song. The café's pianist worked with him.
arc.sourceNote: Summary, not a located composition day. User-authorized short source-led vignette; FOR OWNER READING, not approved.

arc.canonicalText: In his memory, competition between the cafés pushed him toward writing a song of his own. A rival song was already a hit.
arc.sourceNote: Competitive impetus, not a documented emotional low; explicit structural exception. User-authorized short source-led vignette; FOR OWNER READING, not approved.

arc.canonicalText: He and the pianist made a song together, with words by one and music by the other. He supplied the words.
arc.sourceNote: Actual collaboration, summarized without invented mechanics. User-authorized short source-led vignette; FOR OWNER READING, not approved.

arc.canonicalText: The result was a collaboration, not a song he had made entirely alone. His partner supplied the music.
arc.sourceNote: No separate failed intermediate effort is documented in the retained primary account; this role is a brief division-of-work summary. User-authorized short source-led vignette; FOR OWNER READING, not approved.

arc.canonicalText: Their song was published, with both men's contributions credited on the sheet music. It was his first publication.
arc.sourceNote: Documented publication, not an invented acceptance encounter. User-authorized short source-led vignette; FOR OWNER READING, not approved.

arc.canonicalText: The song did not become a hit, and he remembered being surprised by its small return. The profit was less than a dollar.
arc.sourceNote: Remembered result, no claim of continued employment or a cure. User-authorized short source-led vignette; FOR OWNER READING, not approved.

arc.canonicalText:
His name was Irving Berlin.

He wrote songs for singers, musical theatre, and films.

Your life is not theirs.

But a piece of this story may still sit beside you.

You are allowed to value a beginning that brought little reward.

You are allowed to need other people.
arc.sourceNote: Permission, not advice or a promised reward. User-authorized short source-led vignette; FOR OWNER READING, not approved.
